body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: fc2b5051069312422de16187f6622f455dfcf16c -->
**Independent review (static, for the v0.14.0 cut): one BLOCKING item. The geometry itself is sound.**

### BLOCKING: real threading programs are not simulated. They fail with a misleading refusal.

The Threading op's kernel (`motion::turning::thread`, the `b.push_arc(..., center, true)` loop) writes each pass as half-turn **helical XY arcs about the spindle**. On those arcs, `f.point`/`f.antipode` alternate sides at each half pitch. In the field, `field_cut::chords` turns an XY arc into 3D chords, and every chord goes through `LatheSweep::of`, which calls `chord_in_meridian`. A chord between two azimuths sits about rho·sin(dθ) off one meridian: millimetres against the 1e-6 limit. The scenario: a TD-0866-60 thread op, then open the field view. It errors with *"lathe chord ... is skewed ... off one meridian of the spindle"* instead of cutting the V.

On main the same program got the named `LATHE_BLADE_REFUSAL` at plan time. So this PR does two things:
- It replaces a refusal by name with a refusal that blames the geometry ("skewed chord") for what is really an unsupported program kind.
- Its Changelog line ("cuts ... threading ... tools with their true blade profile") claims something the shipped op cannot do. Only the synthetic axial passes in `stock_lathe_blade.rs::a_thread_pass_cuts_its_truncated_v` are cut. No app-level test runs a generated Threading op through `field_view_with`; `lathe_field_sim` covers only GrooveRough.

Revolving the helix would not be right either. The revolved reading of a helical pass removes a full ring at every station, so the picture would show the crests gone (material removed that the tool left). That is exactly the direction to avoid. Either fix closes this:
- (a) keep a named refusal for a Thread tool, or for any arc in a turning program, in `lathe_plan`, and narrow the changelog to groove/part and form; or
- (b) model the thread properly and pin it with an app-level Threading-op test.

### Checked and fine
- **No under-cut, no over-claim.** The Blade is an inset rectangle dilated by `corner`, which is exactly the rounded rectangle. The Thread is an exact polygon. The Form crown has its chord vertices on the arc. The solid is convex and sits on the circle's centre side, so the polygon is inscribed and under-reads by at most 1e-4 (`CROWN_SAG_TOL`). The swept solid is the hull of the polygon at both chord ends, which is the Minkowski sum for a convex polygon and a segment. `sd_convex` uses CCW orientation and matches the monotone chain's output order.
- **Conventions match the kernels.** `turning::blade` puts the tip at the band centre. `turning::form` uses `tip = max(E − sag(x − c))`, so the crown's lowest point is at the tip. Both match `profile_of` and #103's rapid law.
- **Part-off past centre.** `r1` is signed against `ra`, and the polygon is added in signed r, so the body stays on the approach side. Reading both signs of rho revolves it correctly. The kernel's own parting rung stops at tip 0.0, so the past-centre case only comes from hand-made programs, and it is right there too.
- **Body height = `flute_len`.** Every feed reaches the stock from outside (the kerf trail covers everything above the tip), so a finite body only drops material a rapid through steel would have had to reach, and that is the rapid verdict's job. Catalog blades carry `flute_len` 8. A user tool with 0 is refused by name ("blade height 0 ...").
- **Nose programs are unchanged.** The bare-chord branch is kept, `round = nose`, and `reach = hypot(0,0) + nose = nose`, so the window pad and extent equal the old `nose`. No golden changed.
- **The verdict still refuses lathe programs.** `LATHE_VERDICT_REFUSAL` is untouched and still asserted in the renamed groove test.
- No unwrap/expect/panic in the new code. `field_blade` is 224 lines and `backend.rs` went from 455 to 410. `field_cut.rs` was already at 443 and is now 446.

Non-blocking nits:
- `profile_of` uses `tool.corner_r.min(0.5 * tool.width)`. With a NaN `corner_r`, `f64::min` returns the other operand, so the blade silently gets a full-round corner. With an oversize corner it clamps instead of refusing. Passing the raw `corner_r` through to `footprint()` would refuse both by name.
- The Form fallback to a plain rectangle when `width > 2·nose_radius` over-claims removal. It is moot while the form kernel refuses that tool, but the "never under-claims" comment describes the opposite of what the conservative side is here.

Back to draft: fixing the fc2b505 review (helical threading BLOCKER + the two profile_of nits) and merging origin/main (RECOMMENDED.md / field_cut.rs conflicts). Pushes follow; the PR stays a draft for the owner's review.

Review fixes for fc2b505, pushed as 5a044ce (plus merge 065e7b3 of origin/main at 75d1b30):

- **BLOCKER (helical threading), option (a):** `stock_sim::lathe::lathe_plan` now refuses, at plan time by the op's name, any turning program with an arc whose plane does not hold the fitted spindle line - `LATHE_THREAD_REFUSAL` for a thread tool, `LATHE_HELIX_REFUSAL` for any other tool. No "skewed chord" from inside the walk, no revolved rings of crests. Axial (meridian) thread passes are still cut with the V. Pinned by `lathe_field_tools::a_generated_threading_op_refuses_the_field_by_name` (a generated TD-1732-60 Threading op through `field_view_with`; with the gate disabled it fails with the old "skewed 1.578e0 mm" error) and `a_generated_form_op_cuts_its_crown_on_the_field` (a generated FormTurning op cuts its valley at 8 azimuths, steel beside and under it).
- **Changelog overclaim:** title and `Changelog:` line narrowed to groove/part and form; the body says helical threads still refuse by name.
- **Nit, NaN/oversize corner:** `profile_of` passes the raw `corner_r` to the footprint gate, which `lathe_plan` now runs up front (`LatheProfile::validate`), so both refuse by name.
- **Nit, form rectangle fallback:** removed; a band wider than its crown refuses by name. The header comment is corrected.
- Merge: RECOMMENDED.md took main's; this PR's entry moved to `docs/decisions/21-blade-sweep.md` with the thread decision added as (5). `field_cut.rs` conflict: main moved `Sweep` into `field_sweep.rs`; the PR's `nose()` -> `bound()` change was carried there.

Gates (debug, worktree): camcraft-sim all suites; app lathe_field_sim, lathe_field_tools, all turning_* suites, stock_*/sim suites - green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` clean. No snapshots or goldens touched. PR stays a draft for the owner's review.
